h2: Magnetic particle inspection services for Charlotte: choosing the technique and where MT is required
html:
Magnetic particle inspection services for Charlotte: choosing the technique and where MT is required

Magnetic particle inspection services find surface and near-surface cracks in ferromagnetic steel: welds, castings, forgings, shafts, hooks and structural members. For Charlotte-area work, Atlantis sends MT technicians from Houston, writes or reviews the procedure through an ASNT NDT Level III, and agrees the technique, field direction and acceptance criteria before the job starts.

Choosing the technique. A useful MT quote names these choices rather than just "mag particle":

  • Magnetizing method: an electromagnetic yoke for most field welds, prods or cables for heavy sections, and coils, central conductors or a bench unit for parts brought to the equipment.
  • Current: AC concentrates the field at the surface and suits surface cracks; DC or half-wave reaches slightly deeper for near-surface flaws.
  • Particles: wet fluorescent gives the highest sensitivity but needs UV-A light and a darkened area; wet visible particles on white contrast paint work in daylight; dry powder suits rough or warm surfaces.
  • Field checks: under ASME Section V Article 7, an AC yoke must lift at least 10 lb (4.5 kg) at its maximum pole spacing and a DC or permanent-magnet yoke at least 40 lb (18 kg), and field direction is confirmed with a pie gauge or shim indicators.
  • Coverage: each area is examined twice with the field turned roughly 90 degrees between passes, so cracks in any orientation are found.

Ask too whether the part must be demagnetized afterwards. Residual magnetism can deflect a welding arc, attract machining chips into bearings, or upset instruments, so the procedure should state when demagnetization is required and how it is checked.

"Magnet inspection service". If you were looking for inspection of lifting magnets or other below-the-hook devices, that is periodic inspection under ASME B30.20 by the owner's designated person, not magnetic particle testing. MT does come into lifting work when hooks, lugs, shackles or crane structure must be checked for cracks, for example during the inspections ASME B30.10 calls for on hooks. Atlantis performs the MT; it does not rate or certify lifting equipment.

North Carolina rules. The state's boiler authority is the Boiler Safety Bureau of the North Carolina Department of Labor, and MT on boiler repair welds becomes part of the repair record that inspectors review. North Carolina also runs its own OSHA-approved State Plan covering most private-sector workplaces, so state rules govern crane and hoist inspection programs at plants and job sites in the Charlotte area.

MT or PT? On ferromagnetic steel, MT is usually faster and better at tight cracks on rough welds, and it can find flaws just below the surface. Penetrant is the choice for stainless steel, aluminum and other non-magnetic material, or where the geometry stops a yoke from seating.

The method is described on the magnetic particle testing page, weld scopes on weld inspection services, and mixed-method work under conventional NDT. Technicians can take MT training and practice on the Practical NDT magnetic particle simulator, with local details on the Charlotte NDT training page. To scope a job, send drawings, materials and access dates through the Charlotte MT request.
